verdicts.decision_note: The client explicitly selects vertical mounting, establishing a case-relevant PCB orientation constraint.

The client delegates PCB orientation selection based on connector-layout quality and makes the enclosure adapt to that selection; updating mounting_orientation replaces the prior value without leaving a stale key.
The client specifies concrete connector-edge, display-interface grouping, battery-relative antenna orientation, and RF keepout constraints for the PCB layout.
The client accepts distributing the connectors along the three proposed board sides while the explicit edge and antenna constraints remain in effect.
The client identifies an enclosure interference issue and establishes that the battery connector must remain accessible beside the USB-C case opening.
First concrete post-revision verification: the client reviews the revision addressing the identified connector-access issue and reports that it looks good.
The critical antenna keepout is confirmed, but the acceptable treatment of components in the recommended secondary clear area remains materially unresolved because it may affect WiFi range.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Horizontal mounting could still work because the display can go on the opposite face. If that orientation offers an advantage, I think it remains an option.

value_updates.mounting_orientation: vertical or horizontal, with horizontal retained as an option if advantageous
